findings.title: Employee counted at two worksites in one month — clear-cut
findings.why_it_matters: The engine counts headcount per unit, so a person appearing at two worksites in the same month is counted twice. That inflates Average Headcount, which inflates the credit. In these one worksite holds at least 75% of the month's hours, so which unit owns the head is arithmetic rather than a judgement.
findings.proposed_effect: Counts each employee at their dominant worksite for that month.

sample.note: Counted at multiple units this month — reviewer confirms which unit owns the headcount (no auto-drop).

findings.title: Employee counted at two worksites in one month — split evenly
findings.why_it_matters: The engine counts headcount per unit, so a person appearing at two worksites in the same month is counted twice. That inflates Average Headcount, which inflates the credit. Here the hours are split closely enough that no worksite obviously owns the head, so this one needs a person.
findings.proposed_effect: Counts the employee at their dominant worksite for that month.

evidence.note: Counted at multiple units this month — reviewer confirms which unit owns the headcount (no auto-drop).
